revisionDesc.change: Finalized - Ready. The new reading on the verso is good. δάνει(ον) is clear and the first five letters of Πετερμ̣ο̣ύ̣θ̣ι̣ο̣ς̣ can indeed be made out.

Vote - Accept-Straight-to-Finalization - Square brackets lack at the beginning of l. 9. συνγραφή could be regularized in ll. 10-11. πρόκιται could be regularized in l. 20. Ll. 20-23 should be tagged as grc-lat. The number in l. 22 should be tagged. In l. 22, dio is interpreted as duo by Browne in ZPE 4 (1969) 45-46. He also tentatively proposes c[athos procitae] in the same line, and to restore the same amount in l. 16.

Submit - There is a docket on the back of this papyrus (find the image here, https://berlpap.smb.museum/04688/) that has never been noted, it seems. At least I found no notice of it in the BL. Thus, I've added it now. 'Petermouthios' seems secure, but what follows that is not. I've added some commentary explaining why I'm hesitant to record Petermouthis' patronymic.

item.p: Just before the lacuna there may be traces of the letter alpha. This suggests the reading Π̣ε̣τ̣ρ̣α̣[νόυφιος, the name given as Petermouthis' patronymic on the recto side. However, I would not print this for the following reasons: first, the other traces before this letter do not fully accord with Πετρ-; second, the name Petranouphis is not attested elsewhere and the reading on the recto is not certain (R. Ast, 05.02.21).
